app/astro.config.mjs:3-5 — current `output: 'server'` + node adapter standalone mode, the documented on-demand rendering setup
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:42-44 — `Astro.response.status = 404`, still the documented way to signal not-found on SSR pages

app/src/pages/index.astro:129, 324 — uses Astro's processed/bundled `<script>` pattern (no attributes → TS + bundling per current docs.astro.build client-side-scripts guide); unprocessed JSON payload via `type="application/json" set:html`, matching the documented split

platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first everywhere it counts (fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, History, replaceChildren, dataset, lazy images) with zero polyfills or hand-rolled substitutes; the only gaps are deliberate omissions (no AbortController/timeout on upstream fetches) rather than regressions.

evidence: app/package.json:10-13 — exactly two dependencies: astro and @astrojs/node, both required (SSR adapter is mandatory for `npm start` serving a production build) and both at their latest published versions
app/package.json:6-9 — no devDependencies, no UI library, no state library, no CSS framework (spec forbids those anyway), no hand-rolled bundler config
dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: the app ships nothing beyond the framework and its Node adapter, with no dated or redundant packages, and versions were current within days of the review date.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:1-70 — all API access, URL resolution, media URL mapping, and caching live behind one module; pages never fetch directly except via `api()`
app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:101-267 — typed result shapes (SpeciesEntry, TypeInfo, MoveDetailRow, PokemonMovesData) at the module boundary

app/src/pages/index.astro:13-49 vs 151-320 — the filtering, pagination URL building, and card rendering are implemented twice (frontmatter TS + client JS), including a re-declared `humanize` at index.astro:137; a requirement change touches both
app/tsconfig.json:5-6 — `strict: false` and pervasive `any` (e.g. app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:44 `api<T = any>`, app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:23 `let move: any`) weaken refactor safety

app/src/pages/index.astro:10, app/src/pages/types/index.astro:5 — `export const prerender = false` repeated in all 8 page files although `output: 'server'` already defaults it; copy-paste boilerplate a future cleanup would remove
app/src/lib/pokeapi.ts:23, 128-140 — module-level promise caches with no TTL or invalidation, so a long-lived server process serves first-seen data forever
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access is well centralized and an Astro major upgrade would likely touch almost nothing (config and one lib module), but the duplicated server/client logic on the home page, `any`-typed API payloads and `strict: false` are the kind of shortcuts that make the next change more expensive than it should be.

findings.issue: Filtering, pagination and card rendering are duplicated between the frontmatter (server-rendered fallback) and the inline client script, including a second copy of `humanize`; any change to filter or card behavior must be made twice in the same file.
findings.suggestion: Extract the shared filter/paginate/URL-build logic into a small module imported by both the frontmatter and the processed script (Astro bundles imports into processed scripts), and render cards from one shared function or template.

findings.issue: `strict: false` plus `any` at the PokeAPI boundary (e.g. `api<T = any>`, `resource: any`, `let move: any`) means future data-shape changes fail silently instead of at compile time.
findings.suggestion: Extend `astro/tsconfigs/strict` (or at least enable `strict`), and define minimal response interfaces for the PokeAPI resources consumed in lib/pokeapi.ts.

findings.issue: Module-level promise caches (species index, types, generations, pokedex data) never expire, so a long-lived process treats a spec-described live API as permanently frozen data.
findings.suggestion: Add a TTL or revalidation window to the cache so long-running servers pick up API changes without a restart.

findings.issue: Upstream fetches have no timeout or AbortController, so a slow/hung API hangs requests indefinitely with no way to cancel.
findings.suggestion: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(...)` (Node 22+/24 supports it) to the fetch call.

findings.issue: `export const prerender = false` is repeated in all 8 page files even though `output: 'server'` in astro.config.mjs already makes that the default — copy-paste boilerplate that a fresh `astro add` setup would not generate.
findings.suggestion: Remove the per-page `prerender` exports and rely on the config default (or set it only where it differs).

findings.issue: The full species payload is embedded via `set:html={JSON.stringify(payload)}` in a script tag; a `</script>` sequence in future API data would break the page (PokeAPI names make this unlikely today, but it is an unvalidated injection point).
Uses `Astro.props` without an `interface Props`, inconsistent with the other components that document their prop contract (PokemonCard.astro, Section.astro, EvolutionNode.astro).
findings.suggestion: Add an `interface Props { path?: string }` for consistency with the rest of the codebase.

summary: This is a notably forward-looking app: it pins the exact latest Astro release (7.4.4, two days old at review time) and the latest Node adapter, uses only current documented APIs with zero deprecated or v7-removed surface, reaches for the platform (fetch, URLSearchParams, History, replaceChildren, lazy images) before any library, and carries just two dependencies. Data access is cleanly centralized behind one module, which would make framework upgrades cheap. The main aging risks are self-inflicted: duplicated server/client filter logic on the home page, `strict: false` with `any` at the API boundary, and caches that never expire.
